Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry & timeline

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with dedicated capacity for our inference traffic (real-time clinical triage). A few constraints on our side:
- Primary region: us-east-1, with EU failover (eu-west-1) for peak windows.
- Typical traffic baseline: 400 qps (short-text classification), spiking to ~2,500 qps for 10-15 minute windows during morning batch jobs.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 150ms for the real-time path.
- Data residency & KMS: customer-managed keys required.

Can you share a scoped proposal for: pool sizing (nodes + GPU type), autoscale/burst policy recommendation, and an implementation timeline? Also loop in procurement and ops contacts for PO.

I'll attach the intake form and a draft PO.

Thanks,
Ellen

Kimberly — looping you in. Key technical notes from infra:
- Given the spike shape (short 10-15m bursts to 2.5k qps), recommend mixed-node pool: baseline 8 nodes with A100-80GB for steady-state, plus a 4-node H100 hot pool that can be warmed for sub-1s cold-starts.
- Autoscale policy idea: target CPU/GPU util ~55-65% at baseline; scale up if queue latency > 30ms for >60s. Allow burst policy to use Hosted Overflow (subject to contract) for short peaks beyond reserved capacity.
- KV cache + prefix caching will reduce token work for repeated prompts; propose pre-warming policy during expected morning windows.
- Network: need VPC peering + own KMS key; ask Security for SOC2 evidence (Naomi).

Attachments: tentative SOW template (I can draft) and a pool-sizing calc.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry & timeline

Hi Ellen —

Appreciate the details — we can absolutely support the pattern you've described. High-level proposal below (this will be the basis for the SOW):

1) Initial committed staging pool (week 0–2):
- Region: us-east-1 primary. EU (eu-west-1) configured as cross-region failover for session-level routing.
- Nodes: 8 x A100-80GB nodes for baseline steady-state; 4 x H100 nodes reserved as hot pool that we will keep partially warmed.
- Expected steady throughput: ~450–600 qps with 95th < 120ms (depends on prompt length & batch settings).

2) Autoscale & burst policy:
- Autoscale thresholds: scale up when queue latency > 25ms sustained for 45s or GPU util > 70% for 60s. Scale-down with a 5-minute cool-down.
- Burst behavior: short bursts (<20 minutes) will be served by H100 hot pool first, then overflow to Redwood Hosted Overflow if pool limit is reached (documented fallback, billed at burst rate).
- Pre-warm window: enable scheduled pre-warm 20 minutes before expected morning peaks.

3) Security & compliance:
- Support customer KMS integration via customer-managed keys (we'll provide KMS integration instructions and proof items). Naomi to provide SOC2 artifacts and an evidence pack.

4) Timeline (target):
- Day 0–3: intake + networking (VPC peering, KMS setup), procurement PO processed.
- Day 4–10: pool provisioning + staging validation (traffic replay, latency tests, KV cache tuning).
- Day 11–14: cutover to steady-state with canary traffic and rollback plan.

Next steps: please confirm procurement contact and desired committed # of hours/month for reserved capacity (we'll size exact node counts if you want a smaller initial commit, we can still provision H100 hot nodes as burst-only). I'll coordinate a kickoff call (30m) with Marcus (solutions), Priya (CS), and Naomi (security).

Thanks — looking forward to getting Aurora live.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
